800 football pitches' worth of new woodland planned for South Downs

25th November
South Downs National Park
Woodland
Environment
By Charlie Harrison Live Reporter

Share

1 comment
Read More

to Brighton for the first time in 2027
(Image: Richard Murray)

0:00 / 1:22
Instaread

A major new woodland could soon take root as part of an ambitious climate project.

The South Downs National Park Authority has announced plans to create 500 hectares of woodland across Hampshire and Sussex -  roughly the size of 800 football pitches.

The new woodland is expected to capture 100,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide over the next 25 years.

Nick Heasman, head of natural capital at the South Downs National Park Authority, said: "Trees are vital ecological powerhouses.

"They provide much-needed habitats for wildlife, provide clean air for us to breathe, enrich our soils, support water drainage, filter pollution and are amazing at capturing carbon.

"Woodlands are vital national infrastructure and national parks have a huge role to play in delivering this support network that will help us meet the challenges of a rapidly changing climate, as well as other issues such as soil degeneration, drought, flooding and pollution."

The project is being launched during National Tree Week and will encourage landowners to put forward sites for large-scale tree planting.

A spokesman for the park authority said the scheme will offset the same amount of carbon as the annual emissions of 54,000 petrol cars.

Supported by Legal & General, the project is being run alongside the South Downs Trust's Trees for the Downs campaign which will plant almost 15,000 trees across 16 sites this winter.
